memory_update.text: MIDD should remain the reference public equipment anchor for restaurant kitchen automation and commercial foodservice equipment, but not dominate the underfollowed lane.
PAR is a small-cap underfollowed candidate for restaurant labor-productivity software, QSR data, POS, ordering, loyalty, back-office, and drive-thru-adjacent workflow integration.
VYX is a messy but plausible underfollowed infrastructure candidate for restaurant POS, kitchen production, payments, and operating-cost reduction after its post-spin transformation.
TACT is a below-300M speculative exception with unusually direct exposure to back-of-house food-safety automation, labeling, temperature monitoring, HACCP workflows, and brand-standard compliance.

Layer 2 should verify customer evidence: named QSR chains, franchisee ROI, multi-unit rollouts, ARR or recurring-service attach rate, service-network density, and whether these tools reduce labor minutes or increase peak-hour throughput.

node: Kitchen automation, beverage equipment, fry stations, ovens, drive-thru throughput, and labor-scheduling tools
summary: Layer 1B expands the restaurant labor-productivity and kitchen-automation node into a focused public-company universe. The strongest direct public-market mappings are not humanoid robotics, but commercial kitchen equipment, QSR workflow software, POS/kitchen production systems, drive-thru tooling, and back-of-house food-safety automation. The two-lane funnel keeps Middleby as the reference equipment anchor, while the underfollowed lane emphasizes PAR Technology and NCR Voyix as restaurant operating-system vendors and TransAct Technologies as a micro-cap speculative shadow tied to back-of-house automation, labeling, temperature monitoring, HACCP, and brand-standard compliance.
